item.title: Radar-based signs coming to Richmond gateway corridors
item.description: The Richmond Department of Transportation (DOT) has started construction on 15 permanent speed feedback signs along key gateway entrances into the city in an effort to reduce speeding.

item.title: Gov. Spanberger issues proclamation to honor Black History Month centennial
item.description: Governor Abigail Spanberger issued a proclamation on Friday to recognize February 2026 as the 100th anniversary of Black History Month.

item.title: First Black county attorney in Prince George is not new to making history
item.description: After its more than three century history, Prince George County has appointed its first Black County Attorney.

item.title: Virginia lawmakers send bill to increase hourly minimum wage to Spanberger
item.description: A raise could be on the way for hardworking Virginians.

item.title: Virginia State Police search for pickup truck involved in fiery I-64 crash in Augusta County
item.description: Virginia State Police are looking for a white pickup truck that was involved in a fiery crash with a tractor-trailer and another vehicle on Interstate 64 in Augusta County on Thursday.

item.title: 28-year-old JMU student dies after early morning apartment fire off campus
item.description: A 28-year-old James Madison University (JMU) student is dead after a fire broke out in an off-campus apartment early Friday morning.

item.title: ‘Dignity does not fluctuate with citizenship’: Local Christian leaders rally for compassion towards immigrants
item.description: More than a dozen Christian leaders from across central Virginia gathered Friday at First Baptist Church, united in prayer and delivering a shared message of peace and solidarity with immigrants

item.title: Dinwiddie pursuit suspect arrested after another vehicle hit by state trooper during chase
item.description: A suspect is in the custody of the Dinwiddie County Sheriff's Office after leading a chase that involved a state trooper crashing into another vehicle on Friday afternoon.

item.title: Dominion Energy addresses high energy bills and offers resources for relief
item.description: If you did a double take when you opened your electricity bill this month, you're not alone. Dominion Energy customers across Central Virginia have reported a spike in their latest energy bill, some seeing invoices that are double or triple the amount they'd typically pay.

item.title: Judge blocks Virginia law limiting minors' social media use to one hour daily
item.description: A federal judge has granted a preliminary injunction against a Virginia law requiring social media platforms to limit minors' usage to one hour a day following a lawsuit filed against the commonwealth by trade association NetChoice.
